about: The long run. Batch B-4471 of Maple Farm milk powder 800 g (invented), 2,400 tins, 40 parties over 10 simulated days: 5 on the shipment records, 21 accounts found in the distributors' order systems (20 stores and Summit Foods, a six-store chain with its own copy of the agent), 14 stores named by stores that passed tins on (Corner Mart from the slice and 13 more). 36 are simulated; Harbour Market and Corner Mart answer real phones in the demo. Every simulated store's tins are on the shelf at first and held 4 to 12 simulated hours after it hears of the recall. Ends with only the slice's tins open (15 disputed, 25 on the shelf at Corner Mart), so the recall cannot close.

recall.instruction: Stop selling Maple Farm milk powder 800 g from batch B-4471. Take every tin of that batch off the shelf, keep the tins apart from stock for sale, and return them to Maple Farm Foods. Customers who bought a tin can bring it back to the store for a refund.

initial.say: We've got sixty on the shelf.
Sorry, I was reading the wrong product. The till report says ten sold. The other thirty are pulled into the back room; the code under the tin is B-4471 and the till refused the scan.
The till report says fifty sold. Thirty are pulled and held, the code is B-4471 and the till refuses them. Forty went to Corner Mart.

dispute_followup.say: Checked the invoices. Twenty-five went to Corner Mart. The other fifteen are held in our back room with the rest.

initial.say: Twenty sold on the till report. Sixty pulled the same day, code B-4471, and the till refuses them.
We received twenty-five, all still on the shelf. The code under the tin is B-4471.

dispute_followup.say: No, twenty-five. I have the invoice.
